profile.name: Satyasai Nakka
profile.title: Full Stack Developer
profile.bio: I'm a Full Stack Developer at Speshway Solutions, where I build real-world web and mobile applications with the MERN stack (MongoDB, Express.js, React.js, Node.js) and Flutter. I own features end to end: designing screens in Figma, building responsive React interfaces, writing REST APIs with Node.js and Express, and designing MongoDB databases. I've delivered a grocery delivery platform on web and mobile, built about 40 screens for a fleet management system as part of a 3-member team, and I'm currently building an event management application.
profile.careerJourney: Working on production projects has taught me to think beyond screens: how admins, customers, drivers, and delivery partners each use the same system, and how to keep one backend reliable for web and mobile at once. Next, I want to take more ownership of how applications are shipped and run, which is why I'm learning DevOps with Docker, CI/CD, and Kubernetes. My goal is to grow into an engineer who can design, build, and deploy complete products.

projects.title: Grocery Delivery Application
projects.description: A multi-role grocery platform on web and mobile, built from scratch at Speshway Solutions, with separate Customer, Admin, and Delivery Partner experiences sharing one REST API backend.
features: Separate Customer, Admin, and Delivery Partner dashboards on web.
Flutter mobile apps for Customers and Delivery Partners.
Product management, orders, and delivery tracking.
Refunds, returns/exchanges, and order cancellation.
Festival offers with theme setups.
End to end: Figma design, frontend, backend, and MongoDB database design.
projects.overview: One platform that serves all three groups from a single backend. Customers browse products and place orders on the web or in the Flutter app, delivery partners manage their assigned deliveries from their own Flutter app, and admins run the catalogue, orders, refunds, returns, and festival offers from a web dashboard.
projects.architecture: Every screen was designed in Figma first. The web side is a React.js application, and the Customer and Delivery Partner apps are built with Flutter and Dart. All three clients talk to one Node.js and Express REST API, with MongoDB storing products, orders, users, and deliveries. I handled the full workflow myself: UI/UX design, frontend, backend, API integration, and database design.
projects.problemStatement: Grocery businesses that want to sell online need much more than a product page. Customers expect to order from their phones, delivery riders need a way to receive and update orders, and staff have to handle cancellations, refunds, returns, and seasonal offers. Running separate tools for each group leads to missed orders and slow support.

featureDetails.title: Customer web and mobile apps
featureDetails.description: Customers browse the catalogue, add items to the cart, place orders, and follow their order status from either the React.js website or the Flutter mobile app.

featureDetails.title: Delivery Partner app
featureDetails.description: A dedicated Flutter app where delivery partners see the orders assigned to them and update each delivery as it progresses.

featureDetails.title: Admin dashboard
featureDetails.description: A web dashboard for managing products, orders, and deliveries across the whole platform.

featureDetails.title: Product management
featureDetails.description: Admins add, edit, and remove products, keeping the catalogue that customers see up to date.

featureDetails.title: Order lifecycle
featureDetails.description: Full handling of an order from placement through delivery, including customer cancellations.

featureDetails.title: Refunds and returns/exchanges
featureDetails.description: After-sale requests are handled inside the platform, so customers can request refunds or exchanges and admins can process them.

featureDetails.title: Festival offers with themes
featureDetails.description: Admins can run seasonal festival offers and switch the storefront to a matching theme for the occasion.

featureDetails.title: One shared REST API
featureDetails.description: The web app and both mobile apps use the same Node.js and Express REST API and MongoDB database, so data stays consistent everywhere.

projects.title: Fleet Management System
projects.description: A fleet management web application for managing drivers, trips, and live vehicle tracking, built with a 3-member team at Speshway Solutions.
features: Driver and Admin modules covering both workflows.
Trip management with live tracking.
Public-facing pages for the platform.
UI/UX designed in Figma and built as responsive React.js screens.
REST APIs with Node.js and Express.js.
MongoDB CRUD for trips, drivers, and admin data.
projects.problemStatement: Fleet operators need to know which driver is on which trip, where vehicles are right now, and what has been completed. When this lives in spreadsheets and phone calls, administrators have no live picture of their fleet and drivers have no single place to see their work.
projects.overview: A web platform with separate experiences for administrators and drivers. Admins manage drivers and trips and follow vehicles through live tracking, drivers see and work through their assigned trips, and public-facing pages present the service to visitors.

featureDetails.title: Admin module
featureDetails.description: Administrators manage drivers, trips, and platform data from a central dashboard.

featureDetails.title: Driver module
featureDetails.description: Drivers get their own workflow for viewing and handling the trips assigned to them.

featureDetails.title: Trip management
featureDetails.description: Trips are created, assigned, and tracked through their lifecycle, with the data stored in MongoDB.

featureDetails.title: Live tracking
featureDetails.description: A live tracking module lets administrators follow vehicles and trips in progress.

featureDetails.title: Public-facing pages
featureDetails.description: Pages that introduce the platform to visitors outside the admin and driver areas.

featureDetails.title: Figma to React
featureDetails.description: I designed screens in Figma and turned them into responsive React.js interfaces, about 40 screens in total.

featureDetails.title: REST APIs and data
featureDetails.description: Node.js and Express.js APIs connect the frontend modules to the backend, with CRUD operations in MongoDB for trips, drivers, and admin data.

projects.architecture: A React.js frontend connected through REST APIs built with Node.js and Express.js to a MongoDB database that stores trips, drivers, and admin data. Built by a 3-member team with daily development meetings; my part covered about 40 screens across the Driver, Admin, Trips, Live Tracking, and public modules, plus the APIs and database work behind them.

projects.title: Event Management Application
projects.description: A full-stack event booking platform being built end to end at Speshway Solutions, from requirements and Figma design through implementation, where users discover and book events, merchants offer services, and admins manage the platform.
features: Dashboards and workflows for event creation, bookings, and date scheduling.
Online payments with Razorpay, coupons, and QR-code tickets.
Real-time chat and notifications with Socket.io.
Google and GitHub sign-in alongside email login.
Merchant services, decorations, and photo galleries.
Reviews, saved events, complaints, and venue maps.
projects.overview: The platform brings event organisers, service merchants, and attendees together. Users browse and book events, pay online, and receive QR-code tickets. Merchants list services such as decorations and manage their payouts, while admins oversee bookings, categories, complaints, and platform settings.
projects.problemStatement: Planning and attending events usually means juggling separate tools for discovery, booking, scheduling, payments, and vendor coordination. This application puts those workflows in one place for attendees, merchants, and administrators.
projects.architecture: Designed in Figma, then built as a React + TypeScript frontend (Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui) on top of a Node.js and Express REST API with MongoDB through Mongoose. Socket.io powers live chat and notifications, Razorpay handles payments, Cloudinary stores gallery images, and Nodemailer sends booking emails.
securityFeatures: Google and GitHub OAuth sign-in through Passport.

featureDetails.title: Event creation and scheduling
featureDetails.description: Organisers create events and manage their dates through dedicated dashboards and workflows.

featureDetails.title: Bookings and QR-code tickets
featureDetails.description: Attendees book events and receive QR-code tickets for entry.

featureDetails.title: Online payments
featureDetails.description: Payments run through Razorpay, with support for coupons, wallets, and merchant payouts.

featureDetails.title: Merchant services
featureDetails.description: Merchants list services such as decorations and showcase their work in photo galleries.

featureDetails.title: Real-time chat and notifications
featureDetails.description: Socket.io delivers live chat messages and notifications to users as things happen.

featureDetails.title: Flexible sign-in
featureDetails.description: Users can sign in with email and password, or with their Google or GitHub account.

featureDetails.title: Reviews and saved events
featureDetails.description: Attendees review events and save the ones they are interested in.

featureDetails.title: Complaints and admin oversight
featureDetails.description: Users raise complaints, and admins manage bookings, categories, banners, and settings, with audit logs of administrative actions.

featureDetails.title: Venue maps
featureDetails.description: Event locations are shown on interactive maps.

projects.title: Vehicle Care Center
projects.description: A vehicle service booking platform that connects customers with service centers, with dashboards for customers, staff, and administrators.
features: Online booking for vehicle services.
Service center, store, and staff management.
Admin dashboard for bookings and services.
Email notifications and real-time updates.
projects.problemStatement: Booking a vehicle service usually means calling a service center and hoping a slot is free, while the center tracks bookings, staff, and services by hand.
projects.overview: An online platform where customers book vehicle services and service centers manage everything behind those bookings, including their services, stores, and staff, from an admin dashboard.

featureDetails.title: Online service booking
featureDetails.description: Customers choose a service and book it online instead of calling the service center.

featureDetails.title: Service center management
featureDetails.description: Service centers, their stores, and the services they offer are managed inside the platform.

featureDetails.title: Staff management
featureDetails.description: Staff records are kept alongside the bookings they handle.

featureDetails.title: Admin dashboard
featureDetails.description: Administrators oversee bookings and services from one place.

featureDetails.title: Notifications and live updates
featureDetails.description: Email notifications (Nodemailer) and real-time updates (Socket.io) keep customers informed about their bookings.

featureDetails.title: Secure accounts
featureDetails.description: JWT authentication with bcrypt-hashed passwords protects user accounts.

projects.architecture: A React + TypeScript frontend (Vite, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui) connected to a Node.js and Express REST API with MongoDB, with Socket.io for real-time updates and Nodemailer for emails.

projects.title: School Management System
projects.description: A Java console application that models a school with students, teachers, and a school registry, built to practise core object-oriented programming concepts.
features: Student and Teacher classes with encapsulated fields.
School class that manages lists of students and teachers.
Polymorphic display methods for each entity.
projects.problemStatement: A practice project to model a real-world school in code and apply object-oriented programming principles properly.
projects.overview: A Java console application with Student, Teacher, and School classes. The School class keeps lists of students and teachers, and the program displays their details.

featureDetails.title: Student records
featureDetails.description: Each student has a name, roll number, and grade, stored in private fields accessed through getters and setters.

featureDetails.title: Teacher records
featureDetails.description: Each teacher has a name, subject, and salary, encapsulated the same way.

featureDetails.title: School registry
featureDetails.description: The School class manages the lists of students and teachers and hides how they are stored.

featureDetails.title: OOP concepts in practice
featureDetails.description: Demonstrates classes and objects, encapsulation, polymorphic display methods, and basic abstraction.

projects.architecture: Plain Java with four classes: Main, School, Student, and Teacher.
